🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin slipped under $82K as AI-spending jitters rattled risk assets, yet ETF buyers kept accumulating while regulators in Washington, London and Seoul pushed their crypto rulebooks forward. 📉 Bitcoin Slips Below $82K as AI Doubts Return Bitcoin dropped as much as 2.9% on Thursday to around $81,600, erasing a late-Wednesday push toward $84,800, after mixed earnings from Tesla and Meta reignited concerns about AI spending and dragged Nasdaq 100 futures lower. Altcoins fared worse: ether slid toward $2,400, while CoinDesk's DeFi index sank 5.6%. Read full story 💰 Bitcoin ETFs Pull $528M in Biggest Day in a Month U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in $528.4 million on Wednesday, their strongest single session in almost a month, with BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC accounting for roughly 85% of the total and lifting the week's tally above $1 billion. Spot ether ETFs also turned positive, ending a five-day run of withdrawals, as investors position ahead of the Oct. 28 Fed decision and the Nov. 3 U.S. midterms. More details 🏦 OCC Finalizes GENIUS Act Stablecoin Rule, Banks Cry Foul The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency published its final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, keeping the ban on issuer-paid yield but dropping a proposed presumption against rewards offered through exchanges and other third parties in favor of case-by-case review. The American Bankers Association warned the change effectively leaves crypto platforms' rewards programs intact, while the Blockchain Association said the rule now tracks the statute more closely. The framework takes effect Jan. 18, 2027. Read more ⚡ Solana's Alpenglow Upgrade Goes Live on Mainnet Solana switched on Alpenglow, the biggest consensus overhaul in its history, retiring the TowerBFT voting system the network had relied on since 2020. Developer Anza says the change cuts transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 150 milliseconds, with a second phase, Rotor, still to come. See details 🇬🇧 UK FCA Opens DeFi Guidance Consultations The Financial Conduct Authority launched two consultations: GC26/7, explaining how existing operational-resilience, compliance and anti-money-laundering rules apply to regulated firms that use or offer access to DeFi, and CP26/36, clarifying which crypto activities fall outside the new regulatory perimeter. Hey Friend! This is edition 100 of Adrian’s DeFi Alpha. Thank you for reading along, some of you since the very first one. A hundred weeks of me telling you to be patient, and Bitcoin still likes to test that advice every single week. This week it passed the test. Bitcoin is up about 41% from its June low of $58k, while the Nasdaq barely moved over the same stretch. Last week it swept down to $79.8k, and the buyers at $80k were buying it faster than lightspeed. The ETF buyers are back too. After roughly $936 million of outflows between October 7 and October 16, the spot ETFs took in about $1.07 billion in just three sessions this week. Though not everything is green. Stablecoin balances on exchanges are at their lowest of the year, and the altcoin froth from September has turned into fear. In the Market Overview I look at a source of support for stocks that most crypto investors ignore: Companies buying back their own shares. And in the Alpha section I explain the investment case for GRASS, with an update on Collector Crypt before that. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Macro Update – US companies authorized a record $1.305 trillion of buybacks this year, and midterm-year fourth quarters averaged 6.6% for the S&P 500 since 1950. Bitcoin is up 41% since June 30 while the Nasdaq is up 1%. 🔊 Crypto Pulse – Spot ETFs took in about $1.07 billion in three sessions after $936 million of outflows. Bitcoin held the 80k–81.5k support, and new buyers now hold 11.2% of capital, up from 6.6% in July. 🐂 Alpha Insights – Collector Crypt earned $25.4 million of gross profit in Q3 on $22 million of cards, while about 44.6 million CARDS start unlocking every month from October 29. I bought GRASS for more AI x Crypto exposure. It trades at about 9.4x this year’s forecast revenue on FDV. The current state of the market. Start with the stock market, because that’s where a potential source of support is coming back. US companies have authorized a record $1.3 trillion of share buybacks this year. Yet in October they bought about 40% less per day than their year-to-date average, because most companies stop discretionary buying in the weeks before they report earnings. 81241.subject: Progmat Moved $2.7 Billion to Avalanche. But What Actually Moved?
81241.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/progmat-moved-27-billion-to-avalanche

When Progmat completed its migration to Avalanche in July 2026, the headline number was ¥452 billion in digital securities, equivalent to roughly $2.7 billion at the time.
Progmat didn’t transfer $2.7B in cash; ¥452B is the total value of securities issued on its platform. That makes the migration less about capital moving between networks and more about changing the core technology underneath an operating financial market.
Progmat’s previous architecture was built on R3’s Corda 5, an enterprise distributed-ledger technology. It has since moved to a dedicated Avalanche L1, migrating its existing smart-contract functionality into an EVM-compatible environment while preserving the behaviour and specifications of existing issuances.
The transition was designed so participating institutions could continue using the platform without having to rebuild the financial products already running on it.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
The ¥452 billion did not “move” in the crypto sense
When Datachain announced the original migration plan in February, it described more than ¥439.6 billion in digital securities on Progmat ST. By the time the migration was completed, the figure reported by Avalanche had risen above ¥452 billion in total asset value.
For a crypto user, “moving assets to another chain” normally implies a transaction: burn here, mint there, bridge there, or transfer tokens from one wallet to another.
A tokenized bond remains connected to the underlying financial instrument and the legal rights associated with it. Changing the distributed ledger used to record and administer that instrument does not, by itself, change the bond.
The closer analogy is a financial institution modernizing its core technology while keeping its customer-facing services running. Commonwealth Bank of Australia, for example, has undertaken large-scale modernization of core banking infrastructure by moving critical systems to cloud infrastructure. Customers don’t need to understand the technology behind their accounts; the bank’s job is to upgrade it without disrupting reliable services.
That is the paradox of critical financial infrastructure: the more successful the migration, the less visible it can be.
Rebuilding the infrastructure underneath the securities
One of the more important pieces of the architecture is the mediation layer between Progmat’s applications and the underlying blockchain infrastructure.
Its purpose is to separate the financial services and business logic from the specific ledger supporting them. Rather than designing every application around one blockchain, Progmat can introduce an abstraction between its applications and the networks underneath them.
